item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Opioid

lookback_source.quote: N0415H1. Opioid: Check if an opioid medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period ending on the ARD; if the resident has been in the facility less than 7 days, the window is since admission/entry or reentry. The manual uses "7-day look-back period" (N0415H1) and "observation period"/"7-day observation period" (N0415H2, N0415 Coding Instructions) interchangeably for the same window.

coding_levels.label: Opioid — Is taking (Column 1)
coding_levels.definition: Check if an opioid medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415H1. Opioid: Check if an opioid medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Opioid — Indication noted (Column 2)
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all opioid medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415H2. Opioid: Check if there is an indication noted for all opioid medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415H1 if an opioid medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415H1. Opioid: Check if an opioid medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415H2 only if there is an indication noted for ALL opioid medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415H2. Opioid: Check if there is an indication noted for all opioid medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (indication noted) is coded only if Column 1 is checked.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period; e.g., a fentanyl patch applied on days 1, 4, and 7 of the 7-day look-back period means N0415H Opioid would be checked.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period. For example, if, during the 7-day look-back period, a fentanyl patch was applied on days 1, 4, and 7, N0415H Opioid would be checked, because the application occurred during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are not counted as medications for this item.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1, None of the above, if none of the listed medications (including opioids) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Medical record documentation that the medication was received by the resident and documentation of the indication for its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Supports both Column 1 (is taking) and Column 2 (indication noted).

federal.criterion: Documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received the medication while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., medication given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.criterion: The indication must be the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box; drives whether Column 2 may be checked.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0 (e.g., a consistently used reference resource, manufacturer's package insert, or the pharmacist).

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as "may wish to"; use of listed resources is not required for MDS completion (p. N-12).

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415H to any payment or case-mix classification.
